key_insight: An explicit, resource-efficient block-encoding enables quantum linear-system solvers for finite element analysis of 2D isotropic linear elastic materials.
engineering_relevance: The framework could accelerate displacement and strain-energy calculations under suitable conditions for polynomial quantum speedups.
method: Analytically diagonalize the element stiffness matrix and factorize global finite element assembly.
Block-encode the normalized, shifted global stiffness matrix using constant ancilla qubits and gate complexity logarithmic in the degrees of freedom.
Apply a quantum singular value transformation–based linear-system solver and analyze selected output costs.
evidence_signal: Numerical cantilever-beam experiments verify the proposed quantum circuits and show agreement with conventional finite element solutions.
watch_item: Efficient block-encoding alone does not guarantee end-to-end speedup; displacement-state preparation and output reconstruction costs must also be considered.
paper_title: Quantum algorithmic framework for finite element analysis of isotropic linear elastic materials via efficient block-encoding
